meta.title: Pinning
meta.description: Which items stay in view once they scroll past, what decides that, and how the pinned strip is ordered.

basics.intro: Something important that has scrolled out of sight is still important. Pinning keeps such items in a strip at the top of the scroller, in the order they would have had in the shift, and drops them again when they scroll back into view.
basics.which: Three things decide whether an item pins:
points: item.pinned === true pins it for as long as its shift is rendered, whatever the reader does.
item.pinnable lets a single item opt in or out.
Otherwise the level decides, through pinOnPass — a whole rank at a time.

rules.intro: A pin happens when the item’s edge crosses a line: the bottom of the sticky top in the list, the top of the scroller in the timeline. epsilon moves that line, and hysteresis is how far back the item must travel before it unpins, so an item at the boundary does not flicker.
rules.carried: Items from a shift that has already passed carry the carriedOver tag, appended to the tags they already have. That is what the count on the top navigation button is about, and it is computed from the shifts, never from the ids.

points: The strip is a labelled region holding a list, so a screen reader says how many items are pinned.
Changes are announced through a live region, and repeated changes are throttled so a fast scroll does not flood it.
A pinned chip is a button that opens the same detail the card does, and keeps the card’s accessible name.
The scroller turns off browser scroll anchoring and compensates for the strip’s own height itself, so nothing under the reader’s eye jumps when a chip appears.
pinning.list and pinning.timeline tune each view on its own.
pinning.compare orders the strip; the default is the same placement order the shift uses.
The parts pinnedStrip, pinnedStripTrack, pinnedChip and edgeFade are replaceable through slots, and renderPinnedChip replaces a chip outright.
handlers.onPin can veto a pin before it happens; onPinnedChange reports the set afterwards, with what was added and removed.
The pinned set is reset when date changes: a new day starts with nothing pinned.
Pinning is per view. Switching views recomputes it from where that view is scrolled, so the two strips can differ.
There is no limit on how many items may pin at once; a shift where every item pins fills the strip.
